beats.narration_en: A car hits a wall. Real crashes take a tenth of a second, so we slow it down.
The hood buckles and the front folds back. Hidden rails inside fold like an accordion.
They soak up the crash energy over a longer stop. The cabin keeps its shape.
Pillars, doors and roof stay put. Now a rigid front hits the same wall.
It has almost nothing to crush, so it stops almost instantly and bounces back.
The front is meant to deform. The cabin isn't.
